t: This is the equestrian statue of Charles I, at Charing Cross. It's the oldest bronze statue in London, and it's considered the central point of the city. The French sculptor Hubert Le Sueur made it, probably casting it in 1633, while Charles was still alive. Le Sueur spent his most productive years in England, producing monuments and portraits for Charles's court. Charles was King of England, Scotland and Ireland from 1625 until his execution in 1649. The material also names Christopher Wren as the designer, though it doesn't say which part of the monument that was.
